OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 6, 2026 (11:08 a.m. EST audit)

STATUS: Direct, time-stamped Diversion Canal flow velocity/discharge NOT independently verified. The operator's daily lake levels are available through November 5, but these are not simultaneous November 6 readings. No quantitative or qualitative current-strength classification is warranted from these data alone.

OPERATOR-PUBLISHED LAKE LEVELS (Santee Cooper feed updated November 6): November 5 Lake Marion 74.24 ft; Lake Moultrie 74.13 ft; nominal difference 0.11 ft, Marion higher. November 4 Marion 74.23 ft, Moultrie 74.12 ft; nominal difference 0.11 ft. November 3 Marion 74.22 ft, Moultrie 74.11 ft; nominal difference 0.11 ft. Both reported lakes rose 0.01 ft from November 4 to November 5, while their nominal difference was unchanged. The displayed operator values are daily values with no individual observation times. Gauge vertical datums and synchronized readings were NOT independently confirmed against USGS station metadata: this difference is provisional, not a verified hydraulic head suitable for computing canal flow. November 6 readings are not yet shown.

OPERATOR HYDRO SCHEDULE (feed updated November 6; tentative, subject to change): Friday November 6 Jefferies Hydro midnight–8 p.m.; St. Stephen Hydro not scheduled to run. Saturday November 7 Jefferies 4 p.m.–midnight; St. Stephen not scheduled to run. The November 5 operator discharge table lists Jefferies Hydro 4,512 and St. Stephen Hydro 17 (operator-listed facility discharges, not direct Diversion Canal observations; do not interpret as canal CFS). The November 4 entries are Jefferies 4,306 and St. Stephen 0. Neither a schedule nor a facility discharge is a measured Diversion Canal flow rate.

INTERPRETATION (INFERENCE ONLY): If the lake elevations share a comparable datum and the Marion-higher difference persists, movement toward Lake Moultrie is hydraulically plausible. The approximately 0.11-ft nominal head remained steady across November 3–5, but direction, velocity, navigational conditions, and fishing-strength current on November 6 remain unverified. Santee Cooper explains that controlling Lake Moultrie storage and the difference between lake elevations affects Diversion Canal flows; Jefferies generation alone does not prove canal discharge, and no scheduled St. Stephen operation does not establish zero flow.

SOURCES VERIFIED NOVEMBER 6: Santee Cooper operational feed, updated 11/06/2026, including daily elevations, facility discharge table and tentative hydro schedules: https://azapp-lakespublic-prd-001.azurewebsites.net/ ; Santee Cooper Lake Data FAQ on canal operations and hydro relationship: https://www.santeecooper.com/community/lakes/lake-data/ . USGS gauge pages for independent datum/time verification (access blocked during audit, so not used to validate datum): Marion at Elloree https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02169921/ ; Moultrie at Pinopolis https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/02172000/ . This replaces the November 5 assessment.
level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
